units.text: 苹果首款折叠屏手机iPhone Duo上市后不久，部分首批用户便在网络上报告了一项严重问题。多起案例显示，设备内屏出现高度一致的损坏现象，外界怀疑问题可能与铰链结构缺陷有关。
根据用户在社交平台和相关社区发布的信息，故障发生前往往会出现类似症状。部分用户表示，在正常使用过程中，手机铰链突然变得异常紧涩，展开设备时明显比平时需要更大的力度。当继续施力展开后，铰链内部会传出“啪”或“咔嚓”的响声，随后折叠屏内侧显示区域出现永久性损坏。
从目前曝光的照片来看，受影响设备几乎呈现出相同的故障模式。内屏中央折痕位置会出现一条明显的垂直亮线，而在屏幕右半部分还会延伸出一条水平亮线或像素损坏区域，形成非常具有辨识度的损伤形态。
这些问题涉及的设备使用时间并不一致。有些用户表示购买数天后才发生故障，也有人反映问题在开机使用数小时内便已出现。多名用户强调，设备并未遭受跌落、撞击或其他异常使用情况，其中一些人此前还长期使用过其他品牌折叠屏手机，因此认为故障并非由不当操作造成。
随着相关案例不断出现，部分用户已向苹果或运营商寻求售后支持。目前苹果对已确认出现问题的设备提供更换服务。不过由于iPhone Duo上市初期供货仍然紧张，不少用户暂时难以获得现货替换机，尤其是1TB和2TB高容量版本的供应更为有限。
截至目前，苹果尚未公开说明问题原因。业内观察认为，从多个案例中均出现铰链阻力增加、异响以及随后屏幕损坏的情况来看，铰链结构很可能是此次故障的核心环节。一种猜测认为，部分设备可能存在铰链部件装配偏差或内部组件位置异常，从而对柔性屏幕造成额外压力，最终导致显示面板受损。
不过现阶段受影响设备规模仍不明确。许多长期测试该设备的媒体评测人员以及大量普通用户尚未报告类似问题，因此外界普遍认为故障有可能仅限于个别生产批次，而非全面性的设计缺陷。
值得注意的是，苹果进入折叠屏市场后一直将iPhone Duo定位为高端旗舰产品，其耐用性和铰链可靠性被视为产品成败的重要指标。如果后续出现更多类似案例，苹果可能需要进一步调查生产和装配流程，并采取相应措施以维护消费者信心。
目前，对于已经购买iPhone Duo的用户而言，密切关注铰链开合手感变化，以及设备是否出现异常阻力和异响，或许将成为判断潜在风险的重要参考。

units.text: 10月26日，苹果公司将于本周再次推出一波新品，其中就可能包括首款触摸屏版MacBook Pro。彭博社发文称，二十年来，苹果一直不愿将触摸屏添加到笔记本电脑上，现在为何突然改变态度了呢？
触屏版MacBook要来了
不屑一顾
苹果高管长期以来都有一个惯例：在公司准备好进军某个产品领域之前，总会先对这一领域不屑一顾。20年前的智能手机市场如此，随后十年进军平板电脑市场也是如此。今年，苹果又在三个重要产品领域重演了这一幕：低端笔记本电脑、折叠屏手机和带屏幕的音箱。
在大多数情况下，外界很容易看出苹果只是在放烟雾弹。时任CEO史蒂夫·乔布斯(Steve Jobs)一度淡化外界关于苹果将进军智能手机市场的猜测。但考虑到iPod在21世纪初取得的成功，以及当时整个世界正处于移动革命的前夜，这种说法实在令人难以相信。几年后，iPhone便问世了。
折叠屏手机和带屏幕的音箱也是如此。对苹果而言，这些产品最终会不会推出从来都不是问题，真正的问题只是何时推出。
不过，还有一个产品领域似乎一直遭到苹果近乎顽固的抵制，那就是触摸屏版笔记本电脑。

乔布斯曾称这类产品“在人体工程学上糟糕透顶”。Tim Cook(Tim Cook)出任CEO后，也曾将平板电脑与个人电脑合二为一的做法，比作把烤面包机和冰箱合并在一起。长期担任苹果营销主管的菲尔·席勒(Phil Schiller)曾对这一想法嗤之以鼻。软件部门负责人克雷格·费德里吉(Craig Federighi)则表示，触摸屏并不是笔记本电脑的合适交互方式。就连如今已担任CEO的约翰·特努斯(John Ternus)，也在几年前否定过这一构想。
乔布斯曾对触屏MacBook不屑一顾
但是，在四年前加快相关研发进程后，苹果将于周三推出首款触摸屏Mac电脑。这款产品将是高端版MacBook Pro，外观与现有机型相似，但重量更轻，并配备采用高对比度OLED技术的触摸屏，这也是Mac首次采用OLED屏幕。此外，新机还将加入iPhone用户熟悉的灵动岛界面元素。
这款电脑将提供14英寸和16英寸两种尺寸，售价将显著高于目前起售价为2499美元的MacBook Pro机型。
不想影响iPad销量
乔布斯在2010年开始抨击触屏Mac的构想并非偶然，因为那一年正是初代iPad上市之年。
随着苹果平板电脑业务不断扩大，库克也进一步泼冷水，反对这一理念。毕竟，苹果是一家商业公司，消费者同时购买Mac和iPad对公司更有利。让Mac继续不支持触控操作，同时限制iPad完全取代笔记本电脑的能力，有助于维持这两条产品线之间的差异。
长期以来，苹果一直以人体工程学方面的考量以及为不同设备设计独立操作系统的优势，来解释为何要将这两类产品区分开来。但很难否认，如果iPad能够运行Mac应用，同时支持类似macOS的多任务处理功能，将会很有吸引力。苹果在iPadOS 26中已经朝这一方向迈进了一步。
库克将触屏笔记本比作烤面包机和冰箱合二为一
同样地，如果Mac能够支持触控操作，让用户通过手指滑动、捏合、平移、缩放等手势进行交互，也会颇具吸引力。
为何转变立场？
值得庆幸的是，苹果如今终于意识到，推出触屏Mac未必会损害iPad的销量，反而有可能吸引新客户。苹果仍然可以通过软件、性能、电池续航和多功能性来区分Mac与iPad。iPad机身轻薄，设计上以触控为核心，因此能够实现Mac无法做到的功能，也能适应Mac无法胜任的使用场景。相比之下，Mac机身更大，配备内置键盘，操作系统功能也更强大，因此更适合处理要求较高的工作。
在苹果内部，库克和特努斯都认为，消费者已经开始期待Mac配备触摸屏。然而，该公司的工业设计团队仍然反对这一想法。最终，各方达成的折中方案是推出一款能够支持触控、但不以触控作为主要交互方式的设备。
值得注意的是，苹果并没有解决乔布斯多年前指出的人体工程学问题。用户仍然需要抬起手臂去操作竖直的屏幕。这样做仅仅持续几秒钟就会让人感到不舒服。因此，苹果此次转变更多是出于营收和营销方面的考虑，而非取得了什么技术突破。
当苹果决定推进触摸屏Mac项目时，受疫情期间居家办公政策的推动，其Mac电脑和iPad业务销量都在快速增长。再加上苹果自研芯片带来了新的市场关注度和换机需求，这些因素让公司有信心相信，未来几十年，Mac产品线仍将是苹果业务的重要组成部分。
苹果需要延续这一增长势头，而加入触控功能显然是顺理成章的下一步。苹果还意识到，让Mac和iPad变得更加相似，可以降低用户在两种设备之间切换的难度，进而鼓励消费者两种产品都买，而不是二选一。
特努斯正在扩大Mac产品线
为此，苹果将在本周的发布会上着重强调，新款MacBook Pro并不是Mac与iPad的合体，Mac也不会因此变成一款以触控为主要交互方式的电脑。相反，触控将成为一种额外的输入方式，用户可以在适当的场景下使用，而键盘和触控板仍将是笔记本电脑使用体验的核心。
为实现这一目标，苹果正在调整macOS Golden Gate，使该操作系统用手指操作时更加自然。这款电脑的软件将采用动态界面设计：系统会根据用户此前的操作习惯，判断用户是在触摸屏幕还是使用触控板，并据此显示相应的控制选项。点击按钮时，屏幕还会在用户手指周围弹出菜单，而程序坞和菜单栏也针对触控操作进行了优化。其目的是让用户能够在触控和传统的指针点击操作之间自然切换，无需刻意思考该使用哪种方式。

另一个推动苹果推出触摸屏Mac的因素是采用OLED屏幕，以及这一变化对营收的影响。与目前MacBook使用的Mini LED屏幕相比，新屏幕能够呈现更深邃的黑色和更出色的对比度。虽然这会推高成本，但也为苹果提高售价创造了机会。这一策略与苹果2012年推出视网膜屏幕版MacBook Pro时的做法类似。当时，苹果推出了一款定位高于现有旗舰机型的产品。通过打造高端产品线，苹果可以提高Mac的平均售价。
触屏版MacBook Pro也是苹果近年来不断填补产品阵容长期空白的最新例证。今年早些时候，苹果凭借目前售价699美元的MacBook Neo进军低价笔记本电脑市场，一改长期以来拒绝在个人电脑市场低端领域参与竞争的立场。
本月，苹果又发布了首款智能家居显示屏HomeView，并开始销售首款折叠屏手机iPhone Duo。此前，苹果对这两个产品领域都曾表现出不屑一顾的态度。

随着苹果平板电脑业务不断扩大，库克也进一步泼冷水，反对这一理念。毕竟，苹果是一家商业公司，消费者同时购买Mac和iPad对公司更有利。让Mac继续不支持触控操作，同时限制iPad完全取代笔记本电脑的能力，有助于维持这两条产品线之间的差异。

在苹果内部，库克和特努斯都认为，消费者已经开始期待Mac配备触摸屏。然而，该公司的工业设计团队仍然反对这一想法。最终，各方达成的折中方案是推出一款能够支持触控、但不以触控作为主要交互方式的设备。

另一个推动苹果推出触摸屏Mac的因素是采用OLED屏幕，以及这一变化对营收的影响。与目前MacBook使用的Mini LED屏幕相比，新屏幕能够呈现更深邃的黑色和更出色的对比度。虽然这会推高成本，但也为苹果提高售价创造了机会。这一策略与苹果2012年推出视网膜屏幕版MacBook Pro时的做法类似。当时，苹果推出了一款定位高于现有旗舰机型的产品。通过打造高端产品线，苹果可以提高Mac的平均售价。
触屏版MacBook Pro也是苹果近年来不断填补产品阵容长期空白的最新例证。今年早些时候，苹果凭借目前售价699美元的MacBook Neo进军低价笔记本电脑市场，一改长期以来拒绝在个人电脑市场低端领域参与竞争的立场。

units.text: Apple Wants to Fix Safari's Cramped Layout on iPhone Duo
Apple is considering changes to Safari on the iPhone Duo that would give websites access to more of the outer display, although the company has yet to settle on an approach.

The challenge is allowing pages to occupy the area beneath Safari's side-mounted controls without making parts of a website inaccessible. In an Friday, October 23 WebKit post, Apple's Jen Simmons explained that an existing web setting could enable this, but Apple's research suggests many sites would not handle it correctly.

That setting, viewport-fit="cover", allows a webpage to expand into areas that would otherwise be reserved. Website developers must then leave enough space around important content to prevent it from being covered by the interface. According to Simmons, many sites fail to make those allowances on every edge.

Apple is investigating whether another solution could offer developers more control with less risk of obscuring content. A header's background could, for example, span the screen while its navigation links remain within the unobstructed portion.

For now, Safari 27.1 restricts webpages to the area beside the controls and uses the page's background color to fill the remaining strip. This limits the width available for content on the outer display.

The arrangement stems from the screen's proportions. Apple placed controls along the side of the device because the outer display is shorter and wider than other iPhone screens, preserving more height for apps and webpages.
Separately, Safari 27.1 adds automatic two-page PDF viewing when the ‌iPhone Duo‌ is held partially folded like a book. Flattening or closing the device returns the document to a single-page view.

Developers can also test experimental support for detecting the screen's folding posture and positioning content around the device's middle fold. Those features are available behind Safari feature flags, while the proposed change to content beneath the controls remains under investigation.

units.text: Following the iPhone Duo launch on Friday, a number of owners are reporting that their inner screens have cracked and broken on their own (top image via scary_duck23 on Reddit).
The affected units all seem to break in the same way. The screen cracks down the center line of the hinge, and a horizontal block of pixels on the screen is then stuck glowing white.
The scale of the issue remains unclear. We’ve seen about ten unique instances so far, with many posting their (similar) experiences on the iPhone Duo subreddit.

The amount of time it takes for the cracking to happen varies, but obviously it doesn’t take too long since customers have only been able to start unboxing the device since Friday morning. A couple of people even said theirs cracked during the first setup process.
From what we’ve seen so far, most buyers experiencing this problem have been able to return to the Apple Store and get a straight device replacement.

People who bought from carriers may have had less luck, as the carriers do not have immediate stock to give out a replacement. One person said they were told that they must have dropped the phone to cause the damage, and that it was on them to pay for repair.
View all comments

In terms of why this is happening, there is a working theory that a batch of iPhone Duos have a defective hinge component. The suggestion is a piece of the hinge is slightly misaligned, and pokes upwards onto the inner screen, causing the breakage.

Some on social media have suggested that users should not close the iPhone Duo by pressing in the center of the inner display, and perhaps that contributes to this issue occurring. It is unclear if this is actually relevant advice. Officially, Apple has not given any guidance on how users are expected to handle the phone when folding and unfolding it.

While the reports are concerning, it is worth remembering that Apple has probably shipped hundreds of thousands, if not millions, of units already and only a small percentage of people have had their phone break on them. Hopefully, most people will be able to enjoy using their new iPhone Duo without issue. We’ve reached out to Apple for comment, and will update if we hear back.

units.text: For the first time since 2021, Apple will be overhauling the iPad mini with new display technology. It also marks the first chip refresh since 2024. Here’s what Apple has in store for this all-new iPad mini.
OLED display

This is certainly the rumor you’ve heard the most. The next iPad mini will feature an OLED display. It won’t be Tandem OLED like the iPad Pro, though you’ll still get more vibrant colors, improved contrast, and a brighter display.
However, it’s unclear if Apple will ship a 120Hz ProMotion display. The new iPad mini might end up being 60Hz still. Let’s hope that isn’t the case.
A20 Pro chip

The current iPad mini features Apple’s 3nm A17 Pro chip with 8GB of memory. Rumors suggest that this new iPad mini will offer the A20 Pro chip with 12gb of memory, allowing it to run Apple’s most advanced on-device models locally, which gives you some improved voice/dictation features with Siri AI.
Beyond Siri AI, the A20 Pro should be a rather notable jump in performance from the A17 Pro, with a roughly 60% improvement in multi-core CPU performance, and a 166% improvement in GPU performance.
Water resistance

Apple is working on making the iPad mini water-resistant, with a new casing and redesigned speakers that’ll help push out water ingress. This’ll potentially make the iPad mini the first ever water-resistant iPad.
Pricing

According to Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman, the upcoming iPad mini with OLED and the A20 Pro chip could potentially start at $799, a substantial increase from the current $599 starting price of iPad mini. It’s unclear if it’ll continue to start with 128GB of base storage at that price point, though one could hope that the company ships 256GB to lessen the blow.

units.text: As is tradition, iFixit has torn open the latest iPhone and laid its parts bare on a table. It found some interesting details about how Apple might be hiding the crease on the Duo’s folding screen and gave it a 5/10 repairability score. That might not seem particularly high, but it’s the best score the site has given to a foldable yet.

The internal screen’s matte nano-texture cover doesn’t just make it more readable in bright sunlight; it also helps mask the crease by scattering reflections. When looking at the display under a microscope, iFixit also found oval-shaped subpixels arranged at various angles, which the site believes are designed to reduce artifacts and further mask the crease down the middle of the display.
[Media: https://youtu.be/WOVIjFnivJA]

The nano-texture outer layer is relatively easy to replace without swapping out the OLED underneath. If you do need to repair the display itself, however, good luck. As is the case with other foldables, it’s an expensive nightmare. Dust did make it into the USB-C port, speaker grills, and the hinge — making it a bit crunchy. But noticeably less of the glow dust found its way inside the phone than the Z Fold8 or Pixel 11 Pro Fold.

As for reports of damaged screens and cracking hinges, iFixit has some theories. The hinge on the iPhone Duo is incredibly complex, and they suspect part of it sometimes isn’t descending properly. There is also an accordion cable that passes over that exact spot, and it’s near the edge of the battery. It’s possible this is concentrating pressure and leading to the “audible crack” reported by some and the broken screens. Apple did not immediately return a request for comment.

units.text: 知名维修机构iFixit近日完成了对苹果首款折叠屏手机iPhone Duo的全面拆解。在详细分析设备内部结构后，研究人员不仅展示了苹果在轻薄化和可维修性方面的设计思路，同时也发现了一些可能与近期用户报告的内屏损坏问题相关的线索。
拆解开始前，iFixit首先对iPhone Duo进行了荧光粉尘测试，以评估设备的防尘能力。虽然手机具备IP68级防尘防水认证，但测试显示仍有少量灰尘进入了USB-C接口、扬声器网罩以及边框缝隙。其中部分微粒进入了铰链区域，并导致铰链在开合时出现明显异响。不过与三星Galaxy Z Fold8以及Google Pixel Fold系列等竞品相比，进入铰链内部的灰尘数量明显更少。
研究人员表示，苹果的铰链设计整体表现令人鼓舞，但仍无法完全避免微小颗粒进入活动部件，因此并不建议用户在沙滩等高粉尘环境中频繁使用设备。此前也有耐久测试显示，灰尘进入铰链后可能影响内部磁性闭合结构的正常工作。
拆解过程中，iFixit确认苹果在iPhone Duo上采用了一套复杂的水滴式铰链结构。该系统由齿轮、弹簧以及多个联动金属组件构成，能够在手机折叠时为柔性显示屏预留弯曲空间，从而降低屏幕受到的机械压力。同时，苹果还使用特殊导向机构控制各个组件运动轨迹，以减少长期开合所带来的疲劳损伤。

此外，外屏拆卸难度相对较低，大量内部元件都能够通过外屏方向进行维修。虽然内屏模块仍需要拆除大量胶层才能取出，但整体结构已经显著优于多数现有折叠屏产品。基于拆解结果，iFixit给予iPhone Duo目前折叠屏手机领域最高的可维修性评价之一。
最受外界关注的则是近期部分用户出现的内屏损坏问题。自产品上市以来，已有少量用户报告在正常开合过程中听到异响，随后屏幕中央出现亮线、黑线或者局部显示失效现象。
经过分析，iFixit认为问题未必一定来自屏幕玻璃本身断裂。压力集中、灰尘颗粒进入铰链、长期弯折产生的应力累积、生产公差偏差，甚至内部连接线路故障，都可能导致类似故障出现。
研究人员特别指出，多数故障案例集中发生在同一位置附近。该区域同时靠近铰链支撑结构、跨越机身两侧的柔性连接线缆通道以及多个结构边缘交汇处。由于这里存在复杂的力学变化，在反复折叠过程中或许会形成应力集中，从而提高显示系统受损风险。
不过iFixit同时强调，目前尚无证据表明所有设备都存在同样问题。现有故障案例数量仍然有限，因此尚不能断定这是普遍性的设计缺陷，还是个别批次生产问题。随着更多设备投入市场，苹果是否需要针对相关结构进行调整，仍有待后续进一步观察。

units.text: OLED displays are still planned for the iMac and MacBook Air, but don't expect either upgrade to arrive in the near future.

Apple's "Pro and Tell" special event is forecast to feature the OLED upgrade to the MacBook Pro, among other launches. However, Apple's use of OLED won't stop there, as it still has plans to use it on other less-Pro models.
According to Mark Gurman in Sunday's "Power On" newsletter for Bloomberg, Apple is currently testing new versions of the MacBook Air and iMac. Those prototypes are claimed to include OLED displays.

However, while testing is underway, it doesn't mean there will be a launch of those particular models anytime soon. Gurman says that an updated iMac without OLED is arriving in the coming days, while a new non-OLED MacBook Air will be surfacing early in 2027.
Planned but far from launch
There have been repeated rumors of an OLED update to both lines. However, those rumors have never hinted that an update was imminent for either model.
In December 2025, a supply chain report claimed that a 24-inch iMac update with OLED was arriving in 2027. In August 2026, the OLED iMac was said to arrive in 2029.

For the MacBook Air, analyst Ming-Chi Kuo said in March 2026 that it would be later than expected. While earlier reports claimed a 2027 or 2028 launch was possible, Kuo pointed to it happening in 2029.

It's not the only OLED Mac model that has been rumored about. In September 2026, there was a claim that an OLED MacBook model would be introduced in 2029 to bridge the gap between the MacBook Pro and MacBook Air.

蓝思科技作为苹果折叠屏手机 UTG（超薄柔性玻璃）核心供应商，其相关动态备受关注。10 月 26 日，财闻以投资者身份联系蓝思科技，询问苹果增加 30% 订单是否属实。
蓝思科技接线工作人员表示，对市场传闻的比例不做评价，公司为折叠屏手机提供高级结构件，相关产品加工难度大，附加值比较高，给公司带来比较显著的业务增量。目前公司相关产线的生产任务饱满，加班加点进行生产发货，同时考虑客户今年和明年的订单需求，做好了充分的产能准备，可以灵活响应客户后续需求的增长。
IT之家注意到，10 月 10 日，有报道称苹果公司结构性调整 2026 年秋季手机新品订单量。对 iPhone Duo 加单 30%，但总量仍未超过 1000 万台。对 iPhone 18 Pro 砍单 10%—15%，同时对 iPhone 18 Pro Max 加单 10%—15%，iPhone 18 Pro 系列总订单量未变。

units.text: This week, Apple will be overhauling the MacBook Pro for the first time since 2021. OLED, touch support, and a significantly lighter design are expected. Another rumor for the new MacBook Pros has been cellular support, though it’s been unclear if that’s actually going to ship.

To recap, Apple is expected to unveil its first touchscreen MacBooks at its ‘Pro and tell’ experience on October 28 in LA. It likely won’t be a streamed event, just a hands-on experience for influencers and media. At that event, we should be seeing the OLED iPad mini, OLED MacBook Pro, as well as a refreshed iMac and 14″ base model MacBook Pro, both with the M6 chip.
Cellular MacBook on the way?

If Apple were to ship a cellular MacBook, it would likely utilize the C2 modem seen in iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Duo. Even though we don’t know for sure if this weeks new MacBooks will offer cellular, we have a number of hints to suggest so.

In 2024, Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman initially reported that Apple was investigating cellular MacBooks for as early as 2026. Back then, he reported that Apple was testing its second generation modem with these MacBooks, which we can assume is the C2.

Additionally, last year, Filipe Esposito reported at Macworld that Apple was testing configurations of an M5 Pro-based MacBook Pro with Apple’s C1 modem. Of course, this is just testing, but the fact that it was with an M5 Pro chip is interesting given the fact that these new MacBooks this week will debut with the M5 Pro and M5 Max chips, rather than M6-based chips.

Since then, we haven’t had any substantive leaks regarding cellular support in the MacBook Pro lineup. That said, we haven’t had any leaks explicitly ruling it out, either. One way or the other, it should only be a matter of days until we know for sure.

evidence.title: 拆解找出病根！iPhone Duo裂屏可能与铰链结构有关

units.text: 快科技10月26日消息，苹果折叠手机iPhone Duo一上市就遇到大量负面反馈，原因是有消费者声称该手机在使用几天甚至几小时后，就出现了内屏裂纹。
专门发布智能手机拆解指南的iFixit在上周末发布了iPhone Duo的最新拆解报告，其中也对该手机屏幕出现裂纹的问题进行了探讨。
iFixit指出，许多用户报告的屏幕故障似乎都发生在显示屏的同一区域附近，即右半边屏幕的中间偏下位置。iFixit通过扫描、拆解视频和研究苹果专利构建了该手机铰链的3D模型，以探寻造成故障的可能原因。
该机构指出，一种可能性是手机闭合时中央支撑杆未能正确缩回，从而对屏幕施加过大压力；另一种可能性是引导铰链运动的弧形导轨在折叠过程中会高于周围组件，理论上，如果这些导轨未能按预期移动，可能会干扰屏幕。
不过，iFixit并没有确定最终故障原因，但故障区域与铰链内部几何形状的相似之处，可能为后续故障排查提供一些线索。
其拆解重点主要集中在铰链上。iFixit进行了荧光灰尘测试，跟踪灰尘颗粒在拆卸设备时如何进入设备。iFixit发现，在灰尘测试之后，铰链开始发出嘎吱声。
但随着拆解工作进行，他们发现进入铰链的灰尘相对较少，尤其是与他们测试过的其他折叠屏手机相比。
iPhone Duo的铰链本身由齿轮、弹簧和相互连接的金属关节组成，结构精巧，并采用水滴形设计，使屏幕能够弯曲而不会折叠角度过大。
这种设计在折叠屏手机中已相当普遍，不过苹果还使用弧形导轨来控制关节的运动方式，以减少手机打开和关闭时显示屏所承受的压力。
此外，iFixit的拆解报告还研究了iPhone Duo的哑光纳米纹理显示屏。在显微镜下，研究团队发现屏幕表面布满微小的圆形凸起，这些凸起可以漫反射光线，从而使折痕不那么明显。

units.text: The cause behind a repeating pattern in the way a very small amount of iPhone Duo screen cracks may have been discovered, with a failing element of the hinge believed to be causing the most damage.

Since the launch of the iPhone Duo, there have been sightings of cracked screens within hours of its release. While infant device failures are to be expected for major product launches, there is an consistency in the way that the screen itself is cracking.

Observing videos such as the JerryRigEverything "test" and posts to Reddit show the screen cracks in a fairly typical manner when under stress. In quite a few instances, the fault develops at the crease line and spreads out horizontally to the edge.

The expectation is that it's the screen itself cracking during the bend, but there's also another component that may be the cause. If a video by YouTuber CuriousHagi is to be believed, it may be caused by a faulty hinge.

During his own testing, which involved a lot of dirt and stressing the screen by folding the hinge backwards, he tried to close the iPhone Duo, but it wouldn't shut. He then tried opening it back from its partially-closed state, only to hear a loud snap.

Like other instances, the screen shows a large white issue from the crease to one of the sides. However, the YouTuber went one stage further and took apart the damaged iPhone Duo to find out what caused it.
Subscribe to AppleInsider on YouTube

After ripping off the display, he closely inspected the hinge mechanism and discovered an element that had sheared at the same location as where the screen crack originated. It appears to be a hinge element that connects to an upper support plate.

It's pointed out that the hinge in question is a little thinner than the hinges above and below, making it more likely to break. Also, a further check on the hinge shows heavy crush marks on a nearby mechanism that may have played a part.

The underside of the display also has what appear to be an impact mark, probably caused by the broken hinge element making contact. The most logical result is that the hinge failed to mesh correctly, the section sheared, and then hit the display, cracking it.
Still a small-scale problem

While there are reports of screen failures, as well as a commonality indicating they're suffering from a specific issue, it is still a limited problem for Apple. There's no major online outcry as yet for screens breaking in a particular way.
That said, so far after launch, it's still a very small-scale issue.
A broken hinge element in the iPhone Duo - Image Credit: CuriousHagi/YouTube
On October 24, AppleInsider checked with sources we have worked with for over 15 years, inside Apple Genius bars at seven stores. Four of those stores are major flagships.

At that time, none of the stores we polled had seen any devices in for service or returned because of broken screens. A secondary check late on Sunday revealed there is only one instance across all of the stores.
The number will increase over time, but it's not yet clear if the per capita will. So far it's not as widespread of a problem as the sensationalist videos propose.
As a reminder, it's not advised to abuse the hinge of the iPhone Duo by bending it backwards, even in curiosity, unless you're prepared to pay for repairs.
And, if yours breaks, report it to Apple. They do not listen to Reddit, or social media.

evidence.title: iFixit 拆解苹果 iPhone Duo：初步锁定折叠屏故障潜在诱因

units.text: IT之家 10 月 26 日消息，iFixit 已经完成了对苹果 iPhone Duo 的拆解，曝出不少亮点，也发现了一些隐患，这款机型被该机构称为目前可维修性最强的折叠屏手机。
IT之家注意到，在本次拆解的众多发现里，最让人惊喜的当属可维修性评分：这款机型拿到了满分 10 分里的 5 分，创下 iFixit 给折叠智能手机打出的历史最高分。
当然，这只是临时评分，最终得分还要等官方替换配件正式上市后才能敲定，但对于苹果首款折叠机型来说，这个结果已经足够振奋人心。
不出意料，本次拆解的核心重点是铰链，这也是这款 iPhone 最大的技术亮点。iFixit 提到，苹果多年前申请的专利就已经透露出铰链的设计思路，而真机拆解后大家才看到，这套机构比专利图纸呈现的还要精密复杂。
拆解依旧从 iFixit 经典的荧光粉尘测试开始，工作人员可以在拆机过程中追踪粉尘侵入机身的路径。iPhone Duo 具备 IP68 防尘防水等级，机身完全防尘，还能在 6 米深的水下浸泡 30 分钟。
测试刚结束，工作人员就发现铰链开合时发出细碎的摩擦声响。不过继续拆解后可以看到，进入铰链内部的粉尘并不算多，和该机构测试过的其他折叠机型相比，防尘表现要好不少。
铰链内部集成了大量齿轮、弹簧与联动金属关节，同时采用水滴造型结构，给屏幕弯折留出空间，避免折角过于尖锐。目前绝大多数折叠手机都在用水滴铰链设计，不过苹果在这套结构里加入了不少独有的工程巧思。
苹果还加装了弧形导向结构，用来控制关节运动轨迹，减少手机开合时屏幕受到的拉扯应力。
屏幕故障的潜在诱因
说到应力问题，iFixit 已经找出了 iPhone Duo 用户反馈的屏幕早期故障的一些可能原因。不少用户反映，在开合手机时会听到咯噔一声，随后内屏就会出现横向亮线。
值得注意的是，绝大多数故障都集中在同一个位置：两半机身连接线的开孔与铰链中部支撑结构的衔接区域。
工作人员借助 CT 扫描、拆机实拍画面以及苹果专利资料，搭建出了铰链的三维模型，排查屏幕受损的诱因。
第一种推测：手机闭合时，中间的支撑条无法正常收回，持续向内挤压屏幕。第二种推测：控制铰链运动的弧形导轨，在折叠过程中会高出周边零件，一旦导轨卡滞、无法正常归位，就有可能剐蹭屏幕。
iFixit 还指出，故障区域同时汇集了多处结构棱边与零部件，应力容易集中在脆弱的多层屏幕面板上。
本次拆解还无法完全敲定故障根源，但用户反馈的损坏位置和铰链内部结构高度吻合，为后续深入排查提供了清晰方向。
其他有趣细节
iFixit 还仔细观察了 iPhone Duo 的哑光纳米纹理内屏。苹果官方介绍，这种表面可以散射光线，弱化折痕视觉效果。在显微镜下，屏幕表面布满细密的圆形凸起，能够打散反射光，让折痕变得不那么显眼。
显微镜下的像素排布也有新发现。部分子像素呈椭圆形，朝向各不相同，没有采用统一排列样式。
iFixit 援引苹果的一项专利分析，这种排布方式可以降低衍射带来的视觉畸变，进一步弱化折痕。拆解博文里附上了像素排布实拍图，直观展示了苹果优化反光效果的设计思路。
再来看像素布局，内屏前置摄像头上方的区域做了特殊处理。和 iPhone 18 Pro 的屏下红外摄像头方案一致，Duo 把这片区域的像素间隙做得更大，保证光线可以穿透屏幕到达下方摄像头。这片区域的像素形状更圆润，排布也更加规整。
屏幕部分还有一处利好：内屏四周的边框靠卡扣固定，没有完全依赖胶水，拆卸时不容易损坏。外屏同样可以轻松取下，这对维修来说是个好消息，因为很多内部维修项目都需要先拆下外屏才能操作。
再来看电池部分，iFixit 展示了双电芯的布局：一块电池放在后盖玻璃下方，另一块安置在外屏下方。这意味着想要更换两块电池，必须拆开机身的左右两半。大容量电池额定电量 11.567 瓦时，小电池为 7.506 瓦时，合计总电量 19.073 瓦时。
两块电池都采用电控可释放胶，通电就能松开粘胶，不用强行撬取。iFixit 评价，这是所有折叠手机里最顺畅的电池拆卸设计。
本次拆解还剖析了 iPhone Duo 全新的主板架构、屏幕多层结构，以及各层面板独立运动来适配折叠动作的原理。

units.text: iFixit iPhone Duo Teardown Points to Possible Cause of Screen Cracks

Teardown site iFixit took apart the iPhone Duo to see what's inside, how it holds up to dust, and how repairable it is. There's a video walking through the teardown, as well as a blog post summing it up.
Apple’s Folding iPhone Might Have a Screen Problem!iFixit
Watch on YouTube

Before opening up the Duo, iFixit inundated it with fluorescent dust. The ‌iPhone Duo‌ has an IP68 dust and water resistance rating, which means it's sealed against dust. iFixit found dust in the USB-C port, speaker mesh, and bezel, but few particles reached the internals of the device.

Particles did infiltrate the hinge, causing it to crunch, and that could lead to screen damage. The ‌iPhone Duo‌'s hinge gathered less dust than the Galaxy Z Fold8 or the Pixel 11 Pro Fold during similar tests. iFixit said the result is "encouraging," but suggested it's not a great device for the beach because some dust still got to moving parts. YouTuber JerryRigEverything also did a dust test where particles entered the hinge and caused the magnets that hold the phone shut to fail.

iFixit was able to peel the cover layer away easily, which is as Apple intended. Apple made the nano-texture cover layer simple to remove so it could be replaced inexpensively, but you're not supposed to take it off on your own. With AppleCare+, replacing the cover layer is $19, and it's $49 without it.

The ‌iPhone Duo‌ uses the battery adhesive Apple introduced with the iPhone 16, so a small electrical charge loosens the adhesive and allows the batteries to be removed. iFixit said it was the "best battery removal experience" from a foldable to date.

The outer display was easy to take off, and iFixit said the construction is "robust," which is a plus for repairability since most internal repairs have to go through the outer display. The inner screen trim comes off with heat, but there is a lot of adhesive to get through to remove the inner panel.
Apple describes the ‌iPhone Duo‌'s inner display as a 10-layer stack, and iFixit was able to peel back some of the layers to get a look at them under the microscope.
The ‌iPhone Duo‌ uses an unstacked logic board, and it's the first iPhone to do so since the iPhone 8. The single-layer design is one way Apple kept the Duo thin.

iFixit commented on some of the display failures people have been seeing, suggesting they could be caused by pressure, a trapped particle, repeated bending, or a manufacturing defect. It may not be that the display has physically snapped, because a wiring problem can cause the same effect.

Where most of the faulty units are experiencing issues, the hinge has a different shape. The failure spot is also near where the accordion cable passes by and where several edges meet, which could be leading to a concentration of stress in that spot. From iFixit:

To see where the stresses build up from folding, we built a 3D hinge model from teardown footage, patents, and CT scans, then compared it with the reported damage locations. The breaks cluster near the transition from the gap for the crossing flex cable to the central hinge support. The damage we're seeing in photos isn't right where the display cable passes through the hinge, but slightly lower, at a point where several edges meet and change how the thin display is supported as it bends.

iFixit said it could also be the curved rails of the hinge that follow the screen's pivot points. The curved rails may be lifting above the flat plates of the hinge as the phone closes, and one rail lines up with the damage. It's possible a hinge component that's meant to retract isn't doing so, but there's no clear answer. The site has an interactive CT scan of the ‌iPhone Duo‌'s hinge that shows how the supports, cable, and components fit beneath the display for anyone who wants to take a look.

With a repair manual available on day one, an option to remove the outer display intact, and batteries that release with an electrical charge, iFixit gave the ‌iPhone Duo‌ a provisional repair score of 5 out of 10. The inner display and hinge assembly are the biggest vulnerabilities, which cost the Duo points. "This is the most repairable foldable smartphone we've seen so far, and it's still going to be a bear to repair," said iFixit.
The Galaxy Z Fold8 and Pixel 11 Pro Fold both scored 4 out of 10.

units.text: The touch-enabled MacBook Pro will bring with it some changes to macOS Golden Gate, with a dynamic interface that will be better for finger-based navigation.

It's safe to say that the macOS interface is generally geared towards the mouse and keyboard, with touch securely in third place. However, the inbound MacBook Pro update with a touchscreen is forcing Apple to adjust macOS.
According to Mark Gurman in Sunday's "Power On" newsletter for Bloomberg, macOS Golden Gate will be tweaked for finger-based usage. This includes the introduction of a dynamic interface.

Gurman describes this as a system that will take previous interactions into account, with controls presented based on whether the users has been touching the display or the trackpad. This probably means the UI will vary between a more touch-centric version or one better suited for a cursor.
Touching buttons will also bring up menus around a user's finger for quick selection. The Dock and Menu Bar will also be optimized for tounch input, too.
The ultimate aim is to allow users to switch between touch and trackpad inputs without needing to think about it too much.

This is not the first time we have heard about touch-based changes in macOS. References in a macOS 27.2 beta in early October discussed touch gestures and touch-based dragging, as well as a "touch sentinel recognizer."
At the time, while it could've been an indicator of a touch-enabled MacBook Pro being on the way, it may have also been an update to better suit Sidecar.

units.text: 苹果正在研究如何改善iPhone Duo外屏上的Safari网页显示方式。由于手机外屏较宽、较矮，Safari把浏览器控制按钮放在屏幕右侧；目前网页只能显示在按钮旁边，剩余区域则以网页背景色填充，可用于正文的横向空间因此受到压缩。
苹果WebKit团队工程师Jen Simmons在Safari 27.1开发者说明中表示，网页可以通过viewport-fit="cover”扩展到控制按钮下方，但苹果发现许多网站没有正确避开屏幕四边的系统控件，直接开放整块区域可能遮挡网页内容。团队正在研究更稳妥的做法，例如让网页标题栏背景延伸至全屏，同时把导航按钮留在不会被遮挡的位置；目前尚未公布何时或是否会推出这类调整。
Safari 27.1已针对折叠屏增加一些适配功能：用户将iPhone Duo半折、像翻开书本一样浏览网页PDF时，浏览器会自动并排显示两页；把屏幕完全展开或合上后，则恢复单页显示。开发者还可通过实验性功能检测设备折叠状态，并针对屏幕中缝两侧分别安排网页内容。
这些折叠姿态和视口分区功能目前仍是开发者预览，需要在Safari高级设置的功能旗标中手动开启。WebKit称，Safari 27.1继续使用与其他iPhone相同的WebKit引擎和网页技术，网页适配仍应优先采用响应式设计。

units.text: Social media and the iPhone Duo subreddit are filled with reports of Apple’s foldable failing quickly and in spectacular fashion. Some users report having the phone for only a few hours before the hinge seems to catch on something, then audibly crack and break the screen. Tellingly, the cracks all seem to happen in the same place.

YouTuber CuriousHagi was able to reproduce the cracked screen during some durability testing of the iPhone Duo. Then he pulled it apart to try and find the culprit. What he found is that the Duo’s hinge is quite complex, consisting of a gear-like central hinge and two different types of linking hinges.

The piece that broke is one of the links in the middle of the phone that happens to be thinner than the links below or above it, and it snapped at a small notch where it would be weakest. He also found marks where the hinge met the support plate, indicating where it may have gotten caught.
[Media: https://youtu.be/wtP7Q9Io90I]

units.text: iFixit’s teardown of the iPhone Duo is up, revealing some interesting (and some worrisome) details about what it calls the most repairable foldable phone yet. Here are the details.
You know the drill: new iPhone, now iFixit teardown

iFixit’s much-anticipated teardown of the iPhone Duo is now live. Among the many interesting findings of its disassembly process, perhaps the most positively surprising one is its repairability score: the iPhone Duo gets a 5 out of 10, which iFixit says is the highest score it has ever given a foldable smartphone.
Granted, this is a provisional score, pending the availability of replacement parts, but it’s still an encouraging result for Apple’s first foldable.
As usual, the teardown is very detailed, and I encourage you to watch the video below and read iFixit’s in-depth blog post here.

Unsurprisingly, much of the teardown focuses on the hinge, which is the biggest news of this iPhone. As iFixit notes, Apple’s patents had already been offering clues about its design for years. Still, now that it’s here, the teardown reveals an even more intricate and fascinating mechanism than those filings suggested.
iFixit’s teardown starts with its now-traditional fluorescent dust test, which lets the team track how dust particles enter the device as they disassemble it.
The iPhone Duo has an IP68 rating, which means it’s dust-tight and can withstand submersion in water up to 6 meters deep for 30 minutes.

Right off the bat, they notice that the hinge starts making crunchy sounds after the dust test. As the teardown progresses, though, they find that relatively little dust has made its way into the hinge, especially compared to other foldable phones they’ve tested.

The hinge itself features an intricate combination of gears, springs, and interconnected metal joints, along with a waterdrop design that makes room for the display to bend without folding too sharply. This waterdrop design is rather commonplace for foldable phones by now, though Apple’s implementation adds some interesting engineering tricks of its own.
Apple also uses curved guides to control how the joints move, to reduce the stress placed on the display as the phone opens and closes.
About those screen failures

Speaking of stress, however, iFixit has found some possible culprits for the early screen failures reported by iPhone Duo owners, many of whom have described hearing a crunch while folding or unfolding the device, followed by bright lines appearing across the inner display.

Interestingly, many of the reported failures appear to occur around the same area of the display, near the transition between the opening for the cable connecting the two halves and the central hinge support.
Using CT scans, teardown footage, and Apple’s patents, iFixit built a 3D model of the hinge to investigate the possible causes of the damage.

One possibility is that a central support bar isn’t retracting properly as the phone closes, potentially putting excessive pressure on the display. Another involves the curved rails that guide the hinge’s movement, which rise above the surrounding components during folding and could, in theory, interfere with the screen if they fail to move as intended.
iFixit also points out that several structural edges and components converge around the affected area, potentially concentrating stress on the delicate display layers.

iFixit’s teardown doesn’t definitively establish what’s causing the failures, but the similarities between the reported damage and the hinge’s internal geometry give the team some promising leads for further investigation.
Other interesting tidbits

iFixit’s teardown also takes a closer look at the iPhone Duo’s matte nano-texture display, which Apple explains helps disguise the crease by scattering reflected light. Under a microscope, the team found a surface covered in tiny rounded bumps that diffuse reflections, making the crease less noticeable.

Another interesting discovery came from examining the display’s pixels under a microscope. iFixit noticed that some of the subpixels are oval-shaped and oriented in different directions, rather than following a uniform pattern.

iFixit noted that an Apple patent suggests that this arrangement could help reduce diffraction artifacts, potentially making the crease even less noticeable. The teardown blog post offers a fascinating look at the pattern and how Apple may be using it to make reflections less distracting.

And speaking of pixels, iFixit also examined the area above the inner display’s selfie camera. Much like the under-display infrared camera on the iPhone 18 Pro, the Duo uses a modified pixel pattern with larger gaps that allow light to reach the camera underneath. In this area, the pixels also become rounder and more regularly arranged.

Lastly on the display, iFixit notes that the bezel surrounding the inner screen can be removed without breaking, thanks to Apple’s use of clips rather than relying entirely on adhesive. The outer display is also surprisingly easy to remove, which is particularly good news, given that several internal repairs require removing it first.

Moving on to the batteries, iFixit shows how Apple has positioned the two cells, one beneath the back glass and the other beneath the outer display (which means that replacing both requires opening up both halves of the phone). The larger battery has a capacity of 11.567 Wh, while the smaller one is rated at 7.506 Wh, for a combined 19.073 Wh.

iFixit also praises Apple’s use of electrically releasable adhesive on both batteries, allowing them to be removed without forceful prying. The team called it the best battery-removal experience it has seen in a foldable smartphone.
